editorial: Suspicion spirals into a black‑screen lecture that keeps you wired to the edge of the room. Conspiracy theorists become your co‑protagonists as the film refuses to hand you answers, framing every interaction like a hostage negotiation instead of a horror spectacle. Joaquin Phoenix brings an almost wordless, peripheral dread that permeates every frame, pushing the audience into an uneasy witness state. The pacing dips during the middle third, as tension jostles between twenty‑minute strolls and heart‑stopping twists, but that nuance adds to the uneasy realism. If mental gymnastics and grounded speculative drama thrill you, this will challenge your comfort zone.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
